question.problem:
Find the binormal vector to the curve $r(t)$ at an arbitrary point, given that

$$
\begin{aligned}T(t) & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}⟨\operatorname{cos}⁡5t,\,-1,\,\operatorname{sin}⁡5t⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Note that $T$ denotes the unit tangent vector.
question.worked_solution:
The binormal vector is given by

$$
B(t)=T(t)\times N(t),
$$

where the principal normal vector $N(t)$ is given by

$$
N(t)=\frac{{T}^{′}(t)}{‖{T}^{′}(t)‖}.
$$

First, we find the principal normal $N(t).$ To do this, we calculate ${T}^{′}(t)$ and its magnitude as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}^{′}(t) & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{cos}⁡5t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-1),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{sin}⁡5t)⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}⟨-5\operatorname{sin}⁡5t,\,0,\,5\operatorname{cos}⁡5t⟩ \\ ‖{T}^{′}(t)‖ & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\sqrt{(-5\operatorname{sin}⁡5t)^{2}+{(0)}^{2}+{(5\operatorname{cos}⁡5t)}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\sqrt{25{sin}^{2}⁡5t+25{cos}^{2}⁡5t} \\  & =\frac{5}{\sqrt{2}}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we normalize ${T}^{′}(t)$ and obtain the principal normal to the curve:

$$
\begin{aligned}N(t) & =\frac{{T}^{′}(t)}{‖{T}^{′}(t)‖}=\frac{\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}⟨-5\operatorname{sin}⁡5t,\,0,\,5\operatorname{cos}⁡5t⟩}{(\frac{5}{\sqrt{2}})}=⟨-\operatorname{sin}⁡5t,\,0,\,\operatorname{cos}⁡5t⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the binormal vector, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}B(t) & =T(t)\times N(t) \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}⟨\operatorname{cos}⁡5t,\,-1,\,\operatorname{sin}⁡5t⟩\times ⟨-\operatorname{sin}⁡5t,\,0,\,\operatorname{cos}⁡5t⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\,\left|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ \operatorname{cos}⁡5t & -1 & \operatorname{sin}⁡5t \\ -\operatorname{sin}⁡5t & 0 & \operatorname{cos}⁡5t\end{aligned}\right| \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}[\text{ }\left|\begin{aligned}-1 & \operatorname{sin}⁡5t \\ 0 & \operatorname{cos}⁡5t\end{aligned}\right|\,i-\left|\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡5t & \operatorname{sin}⁡5t \\ -\operatorname{sin}⁡5t & \operatorname{cos}⁡5t\end{aligned}\right|\,j+\left|\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡5t & -1 \\ -\operatorname{sin}⁡5t & 0\end{aligned}\right|\,k\text{ }] \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}⟨-\operatorname{cos}⁡5t-0,-({cos}^{2}⁡5t+{sin}^{2}⁡5t),0-\operatorname{sin}⁡5t⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}⟨-\operatorname{cos}⁡5t,\,-1,\,-\operatorname{sin}⁡5t⟩\end{aligned}
$$
